script: I said hello, they walked past—then one did something insane.. I walk the front desk at this mega‑bank, making badges, answering calls, saying "good evening" to anyone who steps in. The boss told us to smile and greet everyone, and I am fine with that—part of the gig. But why do some people just ignore me? I wave, "have a nice evening," and they walk straight past like I am a wall or a plant—no eye contact, just phones glued to their faces, acting like I am invisible. They're like, "I am too important to acknowledge a human being who's literally talking to them." The ones who do reply are usually tech or support staff. They smile, say thanks, treat me like a person. The rest? They think replying to a receptionist lowers their net worth. I stopped waiting for their nods. I just do my part, move on. But I still wonder what they gain from being so arrogant. Do they go home thinking, "I ignored a greeting today—so powerful"? I am studying at a top university, grinding for a high‑level spot. If I ever get there, I'll still reply to everyone, still be gentle and respectful because I know how it feels to be on the other side. Sometimes it even fuels me: "Yeah, keep ignoring me. Maybe one day I'll be the one signing your evaluation." I don't know if I am overthinking. Maybe corporate life is just that. Maybe receptionists are meant to be invisible. But every time it happens, it's a tiny reminder that people choose arrogance even when kindness costs nothing.
